name: Paul Keating
summary: Keating combines open markets and financial liberalisation with social protection, union bargaining and funded retirement savings. He advocates multicultural citizenship, Indigenous native title and a parliamentary republic, while opposing AUKUS and US strategic predominance in Asia.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Defends Medicare as indispensable social reform.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Competitive markets underpin his economic reforms.

public-ownership.rationale: Defends selling Qantas and Commonwealth Bank.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Endorses higher taxation of very large superannuation balances; his 2026 statement separately argues ordinary income is overtaxed.

unions-good.rationale: Credits unions with successful consensual reform.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Argues development markets need stronger planning standards and regulation to protect Sydney Harbour.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: His government pursued racial-hatred legislation, resulting in civil restrictions under section 18C.

strong-leader.rationale: Rejects concentrating representative executive power in one popularly mandated president.

state-harmful.rationale: Defends active government shaping social outcomes.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Argues recognising native title redresses longstanding dispossession.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Retains valued inheritance within an evolving inclusive nation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Favours immigration supporting a young, growing population.

free-trade.rationale: Defends openness and reciprocal market access.

nation-first.rationale: Says he represents Australia’s interests rather than those of the US or Taiwan.

open-borders.rationale: Introduced mandatory detention for unauthorised arrivals while supporting a substantial regulated migration program.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Demands urgent carbon abatement and supports government’s renewable-energy investment framework.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Rejects nuclear electricity as dangerous, costly and obsolete.

central-planning.rationale: Favours competitive allocation over administrative controls.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Defends industry plans and Creative Nation.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Continues advocating an Australian republic with a parliamentary-appointed president.

democracy-best.rationale: Defends parliamentary democracy despite unpopular necessary reforms.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rejects White Australia and monocultural nationhood.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Defends native title and negotiation rights, while explicitly allowing public-interest overrides with compensation.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rejects retreat into a mythical monoculture.

taxation-theft.rationale: Defends taxing real capital gains as necessary tax equity.

positive-liberty.rationale: Says real choice for women requires economic independence, not merely formal opportunities.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Calls deficits normal and desirable when unemployment is high.

national-self-determination.rationale: Defends Indonesian control of East Timor on security grounds rather than treating every nation’s statehood as unconditional.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Reciprocity requires work or study alongside assistance.

class-collaboration.rationale: Accord trades wage restraint for social provision.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Advocates women’s full participation across government, business and professions, challenging established exclusion.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Identifies entrenched cultural and institutional barriers favouring men in public life.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Government must support education and welfare.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Defends equal treatment and opportunity regardless of origins.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Insists economic recovery must reach disadvantaged people and the long-term unemployed.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Praises multicultural Australia’s success and enrichment.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Still celebrates his Indonesian security agreement; objections to AUKUS do not amount to rejecting every standing security partnership.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Praises Suharto’s ordered development but says political representation should have expanded as incomes grew.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rejects popular presidential election in favour of Parliament’s two-thirds joint vote.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Rejects inflation-first monetary policy and demands greater priority for employment; does not reject all bank autonomy.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Defends Indonesia’s annexation of East Timor as a security measure and describes it as Indonesian territory.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Advocates a head of state above politics.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Endorses the caucus goal of half women by 2000, rather than a universal statutory requirement.

public-money-creation.rationale: Defends banks creating credit through lending.

elective-rulers.rationale: Wants Parliament to choose the head of state by a two-thirds joint majority.

minority-veto.rationale: Explicitly distinguishes native-title negotiation rights from a veto over development.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Proposes safeguards removing a president who misuses powers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Explicitly prioritises parliamentary primacy over a separately mandated president.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Explicitly favours workers owning retirement capital through funded superannuation, while retaining the age-pension safety net.

job-guarantee.rationale: His Job Compact guaranteed subsidised or publicly funded work after prolonged unemployment; narrower than a universal guarantee.

non-intervention.rationale: Defends Indonesia’s East Timor intervention as a national-security response, contradicting an absolute ban on intervention.

religious-nation.rationale: Explicitly praises Indonesia’s secular nationhood instead of a religious state governed by Sharia.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Supports publicly financed employment assistance through competing government, community and private case managers.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Links women’s equality to economic independence, employment and changes in care provision.

socialized-care.rationale: Promotes expanded publicly supported childcare places and assistance with working parents’ childcare costs.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: His government legislated protection for private consensual adult sexual conduct in 1994, superseding his earlier opposing vote.

assisted-dying.rationale: Opposes the NSW bill and argues for palliative care and protection of vulnerable lives.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combines competitive markets with social protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Advocates capable sovereign defence with conventional submarines instead of the AUKUS fleet.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Defends nationally consistent native-title rules and judicial certainty over conflicting ad hoc arrangements.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Personally argued in Cabinet to lift the ban despite opposition from defence chiefs and his own minister.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Objects to potentially nuclear-armed US submarines and nuclear-capable B-52 deployments on Australian territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Opposes US military embedding and force-posture arrangements that compromise Australian strategic control.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Calls Indigenous reconciliation spiritual as well as material.

dense-cities.rationale: Advocates compact, attractive higher-density cities connected by public transport instead of continuing sprawl.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Supports pricing carbon and attacks direct-action subsidies to polluters as inefficient.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Condemns failure to disclose military-integration strategy to voters and the Labor Party.

capital-controls.rationale: Defends floating currency and open finance.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Defends negotiated enterprise bargaining with unions.

women-suffrage.rationale: Calls women’s full political participation essential and promotes their parliamentary representation.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Gives the Office of the Status of Women a central policy-monitoring role.

close-ties-china.rationale: Rejects US-directed confrontation with China in favour of independent engagement with Asia.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Prefers individual needs over passive universalism.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Condemns preferential capital taxation benefiting political associates and rejects special startup and share exemptions.

multipolar-world.rationale: Rejects American military predominance over Asia’s own centres of power.

notes: His defence of Suharto and Indonesian intervention in East Timor is recorded alongside his later opposition to Australian involvement in US-led confrontation with China. Native-title negotiation is not an unlimited veto. Superannuation remains supplemented by the public age pension. His support for taxing large capital accumulations coexists with opposition to excessive income taxation. His military-service intervention and government’s 1994 sexual-conduct law postdate his 1973 vote against decriminalisation; no marriage position is inferred from these. No positions are inferred from Catholic identity or party membership.
